changes.after: A program is a set of instructions for a computer to follow.

before: A program is a set of instructions. Java source code is text that a Java toolchain translates so it can run.
Our example lives in Main.java. public class Main names its container Main; the file name matches this public class. Braces { } group the contents.

public static void main(String[] args) is the conventional entry method used here. Execution starts inside its braces. The launcher supplies args; this first example does not use it. We will unpack method inputs and results later.
System.out.println("Hello") calls a printing method. The quoted text is a string value. println displays it and moves to the next line; the semicolon ends this instruction.
Two print instructions run from top to bottom. Changing their order changes the displayed order, not the words themselves.
after: A program is a set of instructions for a computer to follow. Code is those instructions written in a programming language. Here, that language is Java.
A class groups related code. public class Main names this class Main. Save this example in Main.java so the file name matches the public class. The braces group its contents.
A method is a named group of instructions inside a class. main is the starting method used here. The launcher, which starts the program, supplies args as input; this example does not use that input.
System.out.println displays a value and moves to the next line. Text inside double quotes is a string. The quotes mark the text but are not displayed. A semicolon ends each printing instruction here.
The instructions inside main run from top to bottom. Changing their order changes which word appears first.

before: Read one idea at a time.
Apply the idea to the changed situation.
Trace the values and instructions in their execution order.
after: Start at the first instruction inside main and follow the lines downward.

before.question: If the two print instructions trade places, what appears first?
choices: Sea, because that instruction now runs first.
before.explanation: Execution follows the order inside main: the new first instruction prints Sea.

after.question: If the two printing instructions trade places, what appears first?
choices: Sea, because its instruction now runs first.
Sky, because Java sorts the words.
after.explanation: The program follows the new order inside main, so Sea prints first.
